findings.title: Default `queued` datetime is evaluated once at import and breaks JSON task serialization
findings.body: `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is evaluated a single time when the class is defined, so every AssignmentSource instance shares the import-time timestamp. More importantly, `to_dict()` uses `asdict()`, so the dict always contains a `datetime` object, and `sync_group_assignee_outbound` passes that dict as the `assignment_source_dict` kwarg to `sync_assignee_outbound.apply_async`. Sentry's Celery tasks are serialized with JSON, which cannot encode datetime objects, so every inbound-triggered assignment will fail with an encode error when the outbound task is enqueued (or the timestamp arrives as a string and `from_dict` accepts it without parsing). Either remove the field (it is never read anywhere) or use `field(default_factory=...)` plus explicit ISO serialization/parsing in `to_dict`/`from_dict`.

findings.title: Tests never round-trip AssignmentSource through JSON, masking the datetime serialization bug
findings.body: `test_to_dict` only asserts that `queued` is not None on the raw dict; it never JSON-serializes the dict or verifies `from_dict(to_dict())` works, which is exactly the path taken through Celery (`apply_async` kwargs -> task -> `AssignmentSource.from_dict`). As written, the tests pass while the production path fails on the unserializable datetime, so the core new behavior of this PR is effectively untested.

findings.title: Failed AssignmentSource parsing silently drops cycle protection
findings.body: If `assignment_source_dict` fails to parse (e.g. the `queued` datetime arrives as a string in a slightly different shape, or the payload is malformed), `AssignmentSource.from_dict` returns None and the task proceeds to sync the assignee back to the originating integration — re-creating exactly the sync loop this PR is meant to break. There is no logging of the parse failure, so this regression would be invisible. Consider logging when parsing fails on a non-None dict, or failing closed.
